transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… mostly my sleep. It’s been pretty messed up lately. I’ll be up half the night with my mind going, or I wake up way too early and don’t feel rested at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I think so. Lately I wake up and there’s just this heavy, empty feeling. Even being in my condo—something I worked really hard for—sometimes I just sit there and feel like I’m going to cry.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I have. I stopped going to my salsa class, and I haven’t really painted. My paints are still out on the table, but I just look at them and… nothing. Like they’re not even mine.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I… I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve felt pretty low, but hurting myself… I don’t think so. It’s hard to talk about.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?
I… I don’t think so. Not killing myself. I just feel really low sometimes, but… I don’t have a plan or anything like that.
Have you ever had a period like this before in your life?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had rough times before, but I don’t know if it was like this.
Did something stressful happen before this started?
Yeah… I guess when the mortgage stuff became real. Since then it’s been about a month of… going from really wound up to just crashing.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot and feeling unable to stop the worry?
I don’t know… I mean, I worry about things, yeah, but I’m not sure if it’s like… unable to stop. It just kind of comes and goes.
Do your low mood and sleep problems feel mainly related to the mortgage situation?

Mostly, yeah. It feels like it started when the mortgage thing became real… and for about a month now it’s been this really obvious back-and-forth between feeling all charged up and then just crashing.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… somewhat. I’m still getting to work, but I’ve been making mistakes with reconciliations, enough that my supervisor talked to me about it. And I’ve kind of stopped going to salsa class or seeing friends. I just… don’t really feel like myself.
Did these feelings start after the mortgage problem began?
Yeah… it pretty much started after the mortgage issue got real. The obvious up-and-down cycle has been about a month now.
When you say you feel “all charged up,” do you mean you have times when your mood is unusually high or energetic?

Yeah… I guess so. Earlier this month I had times where I felt kind of lit up, like I could handle anything. But I was also getting irritated really fast—snapping at my mom or even my supervisor over small questions that normally wouldn’t bother me.
During those times when you felt all charged up, did you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah… a few nights I only slept maybe three or four hours, but I still got up feeling really wired. Like I didn’t even need coffee.
During those times when you felt charged up, were you more talkative than usual?

Yeah… I think so. My sister said I was talking really fast, like about the mortgage stuff—equity, taxes—and then even paint colors, and she couldn’t really get a word in. I could kind of feel myself just… pushing to keep talking.
During those times when you felt charged up, were you doing a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Yeah… I was doing more than usual. After work I’d come home and just start cleaning or making renovation lists, checking interest rates, thinking up side-job stuff. It was like I couldn’t really shut it off.
During those charged-up times, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?
Yeah… I guess I did. I started feeling like I could pay the condo down really fast, pass the CPA exams, maybe even run a bookkeeping thing on the side. At the time it felt like… I just couldn’t fail.
During those charged-up times, were you ever hospitalized because of how you were acting or feeling?
No… I don’t think so. I’ve never been hospitalized for it.
During those charged-up times, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, financially, or in your relationships?

A little, yeah. I mean, I still go to work, but I’ve made some reconciliation mistakes… enough that my supervisor pulled me aside. And I’ve kind of been avoiding salsa class and seeing friends. I just don’t feel like myself.
When you felt charged up earlier this month, did that last for at least 4 days in a row?
Yeah… I think so. It’s been kind of cycling like that for about a month now, since the mortgage stuff got real. The charged-up part was… more than just a day or two.
During those charged-up times, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?
I don’t think so… nothing really out of character like that. Maybe I was a little more quick to act on things, but I can’t think of anything risky.
